text.p: The Mexican brokerage Valores Finamex said Wednesday it was upgrading its rating on Mexican glass giant Vitro to buy from hold.

-- Analyst Luis Antonio de Leon said Vitro's decision to unload its stake in Anchor Glass Containter Corp and accept a dilution its its Serfin stake "should improve its cash flow generation significantly."

--"Vitro, once a certifiable blue chip, lost favor with investors after strategic mistakes hampered its ability to achieve earnings growth. But the conglomerate has now learned from its mistakes and embarked on a major restructuring," de Leon said.
--De Leon said Vitro shares were seen having a strong upside potential with target prices of $12.30, $16.20 and $20.70 per ADR for the next three years.
--Given the strong decrease in debt recorded in the third quarter of 1996, Vitro trades an at "unjustified" 35 percent discount to the market.
--On a three-year historical basis the discount has been 20 percent, the analyst said.
